question: Does any wall-clock timeout on the generation path truncate token production?
note: No wall-clock timeout truncates generation. Machine speed cannot change which tokens are produced under greedy + max_new_tokens. Canary drift contaminates timing endpoints only; envelope (peak KV / context) remains over all blocks.

notes: run_task calls backend.generate with no wall-clock deadline or timeout wrapper.
context_cap_tokens terminates BEFORE generate based on projected context (token arithmetic), not wall clock.
max_tokens is a token budget, not a wall-clock timeout.
GenerationConfig sets max_new_tokens and do_sample=False only.
Runtime inspection of openvino_genai.GenerationConfig: no attributes matching time/timeout/duration/deadline.
Streamer records first-token wall as TTFT fallback; does not cancel generation.

findings.note: Bounds free-memory recovery wait between tasks after pipeline teardown; does not interrupt generate().
Ends the throughput warmup sampling loop by elapsed time; not applied to timed-task generation.
Process-management joins only; not on the LLM generate path.
Refuse to start a block if the machine lock is not acquired; never truncates an in-flight generate.

implication: C2f §3 stands. Per-endpoint canary scoping is required: envelope over all blocks; timing over canary_admissible ∩ paging_admissible. Canary alone is not clearance-fatal for the primary (peak KV / envelope) endpoint.
